title: Canonical Specification Core
summary: Establish the authoritative, versioned and auditable engineering specification model for all AGASTYA product work.

intent.statement: Provide a trustworthy source of engineering intent that teams can author, validate, approve, version, retrieve and audit before implementation begins.
desired_outcomes: Every P0 engineering change is governed by a canonical specification revision.
A user can determine which specification version is authoritative and why.
Unresolved questions, assumptions and approvals are explicit rather than implicit.

success_measures.name: P0 governed-change coverage
success_measures.target: 100% of P0 changes reference an approved specification version
success_measures.measurement_method: Audit each merged P0 change for a traceable specification reference.

success_measures.name: Specification retrieval reliability
success_measures.target: 99.9% successful retrieval during controlled P0 acceptance testing
success_measures.measurement_method: Run API and CLI acceptance tests against approved revisions.

provenance.rationale: Derived from the AGASTYA product north star and P0 roadmap.

problem.statement: Engineering work often begins from fragmented requirements, chat messages and code assumptions, making it difficult to determine the approved intent of a change.
problem.current_state: The AGASTYA repository contains the strategic product vision but has no executable, versioned domain object for a governing specification revision.
impact: Implementation may begin without a verified definition of expected behaviour.
Approvals and audit trails cannot be reconstructed consistently.
Future traceability and verification features have no authoritative foundation.

business_context.business_value: The core prevents AGASTYA from becoming an ungoverned code-generation product by making approved intent an explicit, durable and testable platform object.

actors.name: Platform Owner
goals: Author and approve a governing specification.

actors.name: Platform Engineer
goals: Retrieve an approved specification and implement against it.

actors.name: AGASTYA API
goals: Validate and persist immutable specification revisions.

functional_requirements.title: Create a canonical specification draft
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall allow an authorised Editor or Owner to create a DRAFT specification from the canonical schema within a project workspace.
functional_requirements.rationale: All product work requires a durable object representing engineering intent.

functional_requirements.title: Validate a specification revision
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall validate each proposed revision against the canonical JSON Schema and semantic validation rules, returning actionable findings without mutating the revision.
functional_requirements.rationale: A specification must be testable and internally coherent before it becomes authoritative.

functional_requirements.title: Approve and version a specification
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall create an immutable, semantically versioned revision when an authorised Owner approves a valid specification with no unresolved blocking questions.
functional_requirements.rationale: Implementation must be governed by a known, approved and reconstructable source of truth.

functional_requirements.title: Compare specification revisions
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall expose a machine-readable and human-readable diff between any two revisions of the same specification, including changed fields and change rationale.
functional_requirements.rationale: Change control requires reviewers to understand exactly what has changed.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The system shall enforce project-scoped authorisation for every specification read, write, approval and audit operation.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Automated authorisation tests must prove cross-project access is denied for each API operation.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero successful cross-project requests in the P0 security suite.

provenance.rationale: Tenant and project isolation are non-negotiable product principles.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The system shall preserve immutable approved revisions and associated audit records for the configured retention period.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Integration tests must prove that approved revision content cannot be overwritten and all prior revisions remain retrievable.
non_functional_requirements.target: 100% of tested approved revisions remain byte-identical after later edits.

provenance.rationale: Approval only has value if the approved artefact is immutable.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The Specification Studio shall support keyboard navigation, labelled form controls and error summaries that identify invalid fields.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Automated accessibility checks and manual keyboard acceptance testing.
non_functional_requirements.target: No critical accessibility violations in P0 acceptance flows.

provenance.rationale: Accessibility is an explicit specification dimension.

business_rules.statement: Only an authorised Owner may approve or reject a specification revision for the project.
A specification may not transition to APPROVED while it has an OPEN question, an INVALIDATED required assumption, or an ERROR validation finding.
exceptions: A question may be marked ACCEPTED_RISK by an authorised Owner with documented rationale.

provenance.rationale: The approved state must be meaningful.

constraints.statement: Canonical specification content must be represented as JSON conforming to JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 and must remain provider-neutral.
constraints.rationale: The authoritative specification format must be portable, machine-readable and independent of any AI provider.

assumptions.statement: P0 uses a workspace role model consisting of Owner, Editor and Viewer; finer-grained attributes are deferred to P3.
assumptions.risk_if_false: A more complex authorisation model could alter P0 API and policy contracts.

bounded_contexts.name: Specification Management
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own the authoritative specification aggregate, revisions, validation state and approval workflow.

bounded_contexts.name: Audit and Evidence
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Record immutable actions and evidence references for reconstructable governance.

ubiquitous_language.definition: A versioned engineering contract representing intended behaviour and governing constraints.
An immutable snapshot of a specification at a defined semantic version.
A timestamped artefact that supports a verification, decision or observed behaviour.

entities.name: Specification
entities.description: The root aggregate that groups immutable revisions under a stable specification identifier.

entities.name: SpecificationRevision
entities.description: The immutable content and metadata of one versioned canonical specification.

attributes.name: contentHash
attributes.description: Hash used to prove immutable content

workflows.name: Create and approve a specification revision
workflows.trigger: An Owner or Editor identifies a product change that requires an engineering specification.

steps.action: Creates or edits a DRAFT specification.
Validates schema, lifecycle and semantic rules.
steps.result: Validation findings are returned without overwriting approved content.

steps.action: Reviews findings and approves the valid revision.
steps.result: An immutable APPROVED revision and approval record are created.

outcomes: An approved version is retrievable by API, UI and CLI.
The approval and content history are auditable.
workflows.error_handling: Validation errors keep the revision in a pre-approved state and explain the blocked transition.

states.name: SUPERSEDED
states.description: Replaced by a later approved version.

data_models.name: Authoritative specification state
data_models.retention_policy: Approved revisions and audit records are retained according to the organisation policy and are never overwritten.

security_requirements.statement: Each API operation shall authenticate the caller and authorise access against the project-scoped role model before reading or mutating a specification.
security_requirements.verification_method: Automated API integration tests covering unauthenticated, wrong-project, Viewer, Editor and Owner requests.

performance_requirements.target: p95 validation response under 2 seconds for a 250 KB specification document
performance_requirements.condition: At 10 concurrent validation requests in the P0 reference environment.
performance_requirements.verification_method: Automated performance test using a representative valid specification payload.

accessibility_requirements.statement: The Specification Studio must expose labelled controls, keyboard-operable field navigation and an accessible validation-error summary.
accessibility_requirements.verification_method: Automated accessibility scanning and manual keyboard test of create, validate and approve flows.

observability_requirements.statement: Create, validate, approve, version-read and diff operations must emit structured audit events with request, project, specification, revision, actor and outcome identifiers.
observability_requirements.verification_method: Integration tests inspect emitted audit records and confirm all required correlation fields are present.

acceptance_criteria.title: An Editor can create a valid draft
acceptance_criteria.given: An authenticated Editor belongs to a project and supplies a schema-valid draft document.
acceptance_criteria.when: The Editor creates a specification through the API or Studio.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system persists a DRAFT revision, returns its identifier and version, and records an audit event.

acceptance_criteria.title: Validation explains an approval-blocking error
acceptance_criteria.given: A DRAFT revision contains an OPEN question or fails a JSON Schema constraint.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system returns a field-level ERROR finding and does not mark the revision APPROVED.

acceptance_criteria.title: Only an Owner can create an approved immutable revision
acceptance_criteria.given: A schema-valid revision has no unresolved approval blockers.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system stores an APPROVED immutable revision, approval record and content hash; a later edit creates a new revision rather than changing it.

acceptance_criteria.title: A reviewer can inspect an exact revision diff
acceptance_criteria.given: Two revisions exist for one specification.
acceptance_criteria.when: An authorised user requests a diff.
acceptance_criteria.then: The response identifies added, removed and changed canonical JSON paths together with declared change rationale.

test_requirements.scope: Create-draft path including project membership and audit event creation.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Passing authenticated creation test and persisted audit event record.

test_requirements.scope: Schema validation, unresolved-question validation and immutable validation findings.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Passing and failing validation reports with stable finding identifiers.

test_requirements.scope: Owner approval, unauthorised approval denial and immutable approved revision behaviour.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Role authorisation and immutability test report.

test_requirements.scope: Revision diff semantics and project access controls.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Stable JSON Patch-style diff test results and cross-project denial test result.

deployment_requirements.statement: The P0 migration must be backward-safe and retain all approved specification revisions and audit events during deployment.
deployment_requirements.verification_method: Run migration rehearsal with a dataset containing approved revisions and compare revision content hashes before and after migration.
deployment_requirements.rollback_requirement: A failed migration must stop before destructive alteration of authoritative revision records.

risks.title: Overly flexible schema weakens governance
risks.description: Permitting arbitrary unstructured core fields would prevent reliable validation, traceability and later executable specifications.
risks.mitigation: Use a closed core schema with namespaced extensions and enforce schema-version compatibility.

architecture_decisions.title: Use immutable JSON document revisions as the canonical specification representation
architecture_decisions.context: AGASTYA requires a provider-neutral, versioned and machine-readable representation that can be authored by people and consumed by tooling.
architecture_decisions.decision: Persist each approved specification revision as a canonical JSON document validated against a versioned JSON Schema; store queryable projections separately without replacing the canonical document.

alternatives.name: Free-form Markdown only
alternatives.summary: Human-readable but insufficient for mechanical validation and reliable graph creation.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Cannot provide a strong machine-readable contract.

alternatives.name: Provider-specific prompt format
alternatives.summary: Optimised for a particular model provider.

architecture_decisions.rationale: A schema-validated JSON document is portable, testable, versionable and compatible with future YAML and visual editing projections.
consequences: P0 requires canonicalisation and schema migration strategy.
Editors must provide a usable interface over a detailed structured model.

coverage_summary.method: P0 initial manual traceability mapping; coverage claims are limited to approved P0 requirements.

evidence.summary: P0 role model and canonical JSON direction reviewed for initial scope approval.

change_history.reason: Establish the P0 governing contract before implementation.

change_history.summary: Initial P0 specification approved by the Project Sponsor.
change_history.reason: The Project Sponsor approved the P0 Canonical Specification Core for implementation.
